clips.send: Under Emperor Xuanzong (唐玄宗 Táng Xuánzōng) the Tang is at its height. New ploughs and water wheels raise harvests; Chang’an (today: Xi’an) has about a million people and merchants from Persia (today: Iran), Arabia, Korea and Japan; Li Bai and Du Fu write poems still learned by heart today. At the end of 753 the blind monk Jianzhen reaches Japan on his sixth try, and enters Nara in 754.

clips.send: The ageing emperor leaves government to favourites. In 755 the frontier general An Lushan (安禄山) rebels in the north-east and captures Luoyang and Chang’an; the emperor flees. It takes eight years to end the war. Afterwards, regional generals keep their own armies and the court is never as strong again.

clips.send: In the year 750, what was the biggest city on Earth? Not Rome and not Constantinople (today: Istanbul): it was Chang’an (today: Xi’an) (长安 Cháng’ān), capital of Tang China, with about a million people, when Paris and London were small towns. The short Sui (隋 Suí) dynasty reunited China, dug a canal longer than the drive from New York to Miami, and invented exams for government jobs.

clips.send: Endless forced labour and three failed wars bring the Sui down; in 618 the Tang dynasty begins. Its second emperor, Taizong (唐太宗 Táng Tàizōng, ruled 626–649), cuts taxes, listens to criticism from his ministers and picks officials by merit. His reign, Zhenguan, is remembered as a model of good government.

clips.send: 大拱（主拱）。一个巨大而扁平的单孔石拱。赵州桥（安济桥）位于今河北赵县，由隋朝匠师李春主持设计建造。主拱只有一个，跨度三十七米多；拱形扁平，桥面坡度平缓，便于车马通行。它是世界上现存最古老的敞肩石拱桥。
